messages:
Aisha (AE): Heads-up — Ripcord wants a 3-week POC to swap CompetitorX for Redwood in their customer chat. They care about prompt/response parity, streaming + function-calls, cost delta, and an enterprise security checklist. Need SE + SRE to run the technical bits.

Ben (SE): I can lead technical POC. Request: sample request logs (200 examples), expected outputs, and a list of features in use (streaming, functions, stop tokens). Also confirm whether they need exact token billing parity.

Dana (Presales): They stream partial tokens and use function-calling heavily. They pin a system prompt per session. They'll share a sanitized sample set after NDA.

Chao (SRE): Security blockers: SAML + SCIM, IP allowlist, cert pinning, KMS-managed keys, SOC2 artifacts. Hosted may be OK for IP allowlist and audit logs, but Private/Dedicated if they require client cert auth or VPC peering.

Aisha (AE): Finance question: ballpark for 1M tokens/day active. Should we position Hosted + enterprise add-ons vs Dedicated pricing?

Ben (SE): Quick parity approach: shim adapter that maps CompetitorX shapes -> Redwood chat schema, and rewraps streaming events back into CompetitorX chunked frames. Watch out for function-call arg encoding differences and stop-sequence semantics.

Ben (SE): Minimal pseudo example (mapping):
POST /competitorx/generate -> POST /v1/chat/completions
passages -> messages, func_call.name -> function_call, func_call.args -> function arguments as JSON

Ben (SE): Streaming: CompetitorX uses line-delimited JSON frames; Redwood returns deltas in streaming events. We'll transform `delta` tokens into the customer's expected chunk frames.

Chao (SRE): Billing note: CompetitorX billed only response tokens historically; Redwood charges prompt+completion. For rough estimate assume Redwood cost = competitor_response_cost * 1.08 + fixed overhead (e.g., 12 tokens per call). Need real traces to be sure. Recommend 48-72h side-by-side collection.

Dana (Presales): They said a security questionnaire (30-40 pages) plus a DPA. I can own that but need Legal to review answers for anything contract-y.

infra-bot: env created ripcord-poc-staging. ephemeral keys issued. Upload location: s3://redwood-pocs/ripcord-staging/ (restricted).

Ben (SE): Eval plan: 1) ingest 200 canonical prompts; 2) run parallel requests to CompetitorX and Redwood (same seed) capturing streaming frames; 3) compute embedding cosine similarity + human accept rate; 4) flag >20% semantic delta for manual review.

Aisha (AE): Ok owners: Ben -> POC tech lead & eval harness; Chao -> infra + network; Dana -> security questionnaire & SSO; Aisha -> NDA + customer coordination. Kickoff Monday.

Ben (SE): I'll post a small smoke curl for streaming and push a runbook to the S3 bucket. Example: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are helpful."}],"stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions

Chao (SRE): Staging IPs for allowlist: 34.198.123.45, 34.198.123.46. If they want cert pinning we escalate to Private. I'll schedule peering window.

LegalBot: Please attach the questionnaire here once received — Legal to review DPA and any subprocessor questions. NDA required before they upload any customer data.

Dana (Presales): I'll prepare our FAQ answers for common asks (SAML, SCIM, logs, retention). Will also note which items require Dedicated/Private.

Aisha (AE): Great. If any blocker surfaces before Monday, post here. I'll request the sanitized dataset after NDA.

Ben (SE): Will ping when runbook + scripts are in S3. Also will prototype the shim transformation and smoke-run within 24h.

Chao (SRE): Standing by for peering and will confirm if Dedicated is necessary for cert pinning.

Aisha (AE): Thanks team :thumbsup: Closing loop for now; will reopen with kickoff notes.
